##### Article 58. Jurisdiction in criminal matters

Article 14 of the Criminal Procedure Act is amended, and shall read as follows:
"Outside the cases that expressly and limitedly attribute jurisdiction to specific Judges and Courts under the Constitution and the laws, the following shall have jurisdiction:
1. For the hearing and judgment of proceedings for minor offences, the Investigating Judge, unless jurisdiction corresponds to the Judge for Violence against Women in accordance with paragraph five of this article. However, the Justice of the Peace of the place where they were committed shall hear proceedings for minor offences classified in articles 626, 630, 632 and 633 of the Criminal Code. Justices of the Peace shall also hear proceedings for minor offences classified in article 620.1.º and 2.º of the Criminal Code, except when the victim is one of the persons referred to in article 173.2 of the same Code.  
2. For the investigation of cases, the Investigating Judge of the district in which the offence was committed, or the Judge for Violence against Women, or the Central Investigating Judge with respect to the offences determined by law.  
3. For the hearing and judgment of cases for offences to which the law assigns a custodial sentence of duration not exceeding five years or a fine of any amount, or any other sentences of a different nature, whether single, joint or alternative, provided that their duration does not exceed ten years, as well as for minor offences, whether or not incidental, attributable to the perpetrators of these offences or to other persons, when the commission of the minor offence or its proof is related to them, the Criminal Judge of the district where the offence was committed, or the Criminal Judge corresponding to the district of the Court for Violence against Women as appropriate, or the Central Criminal Judge within its own scope, without prejudice to the jurisdiction of the Duty Investigating Judge of the place where the offence was committed to issue a judgment by consent, or of the competent Judge for Violence against Women as appropriate, under the terms established in article 801.  
Notwithstanding, in cases within the jurisdiction of the Criminal Judge, if the offence is one of those attributed to the Jury Court, the hearing and judgment shall correspond to the latter.  
4. For the hearing and judgment of cases in all other instances, the Provincial Court of the district where the offence was committed, or the Provincial Court corresponding to the district of the Court for Violence against Women as appropriate, or the Criminal Chamber of the National Court.  
Notwithstanding, in cases within the jurisdiction of the Provincial Court, if the offence is one of those attributed to the Jury Court, the hearing and judgment shall correspond to the latter.  
5. The Courts for Violence against Women shall have jurisdiction in the following matters, in all cases in accordance with the procedures and appeals provided for in this Act:
a) For the investigation of proceedings to demand criminal liability for offences contained in the titles of the Criminal Code relating to homicide, abortion, injuries, injuries to the foetus, offences against freedom, offences against moral integrity, against freedom and sexual indemnity or any other offence committed with violence or intimidation, provided that they have been committed against a person who is or has been his wife, or a woman who is or has been linked to the perpetrator by an analogous relationship

of affection, even without cohabitation, as well as those committed against descendants, whether his own or those of his wife or cohabitant, or against minors or incapacitated persons who live with him or who are subject to the authority, guardianship, curatorship, fostering or de facto care of his wife or cohabitant, when an act of gender-based violence has also occurred.  
b) For the investigation of proceedings to demand criminal liability for any offence against family rights and duties, when the victim is one of the persons identified as such in the preceding paragraph.  
c) For the adoption of the corresponding protection orders for victims, without prejudice to the powers attributed to the Duty Judge.  
d) For the hearing and judgment of minor offences contained in titles I and II of book III of the Criminal Code, when the victim is one of the persons identified as such in paragraph a) of this section."

##### Article 59. Territorial jurisdiction

A new article 15 bis is added to the Criminal Procedure Act, which shall read as follows:
"In the case of any of the offences or minor offences whose investigation or hearing corresponds to the Judge for Violence against Women, territorial jurisdiction shall be determined by the place of the victim's domicile, without prejudice to the adoption of the protection order, or urgent measures under article 13 of this Act that may be adopted by the Judge of the place where the events were committed."

##### Article 60. Jurisdiction by connection

A new article 17 bis is added to the Criminal Procedure Act, which shall read as follows:
"The jurisdiction of the Courts for Violence against Women shall extend to the investigation and hearing of connected offences and minor offences provided that the connection originates in any of the circumstances provided for in paragraphs 3.º and 4.º of article 17 of this Act."

#### CHAPTER IV

Judicial measures for the protection and security of victims

##### Article 61. General provisions

1. The protection and security measures provided for in this chapter shall be compatible with any of the precautionary and security measures that may be adopted in civil and criminal proceedings.  
2. In all proceedings related to gender-based violence, the competent Judge must rule in all cases, ex officio or at the request of the victims, the children, persons living with them or subject to their care or custody, the Public Prosecutor's Office or the Administration on which the victim assistance or reception services depend, on the appropriateness of adopting the precautionary and security measures contemplated in this chapter, especially those set out in articles 64, 65 and 66, determining their duration and their regime of compliance and, if appropriate, the complementary measures to them that may be necessary.

##### Article 62. On the protection order

Upon receipt of an application for the adoption of a protection order, the Judge for Violence against Women and, as appropriate, the Duty Judge, shall act in accordance with the provisions of article 544 ter of the Criminal Procedure Act.

##### Article 63. On data protection and limitations on publicity

1. In proceedings and procedures related to gender-based violence, the privacy of victims shall be protected; in particular, their personal data, those of their descendants and those of any other person who is under their care or custody.  
2. The competent Judges may order, ex officio or at the request of a party, that hearings be held in camera and that proceedings be confidential.

##### Artículo 64

De las medidas de salida del domicilio, alejamiento o suspensión de las comunicaciones.  
1.	El Juez podrá ordenar la salida obligatoria del inculpado por violencia de género del domicilio en el que hubiera estado conviviendo o tenga su residencia la unidad familiar, así como la prohibición de volver al mismo.  
2.	El Juez, con carácter excepcional, podrá autorizar que la persona protegida concierte, con una agencia o sociedad pública allí donde la hubiere y que incluya entre sus actividades la del arrendamiento de viviendas, la permuta del uso atribuido de la vivienda familiar de la que sean copropietarios, por el uso de otra vivienda, durante el tiempo y en las condiciones que se determinen.  
3.	El Juez podrá prohibir al inculpado que se aproxime a la persona protegida, lo que le impide acercarse a la misma en cualquier lugar donde se encuentre, así como acercarse a su domicilio, a su lugar de trabajo o a cualquier otro que sea frecuentado por ella.  
Podrá acordarse la utilización de instrumentos con la tecnología adecuada para verificar de inmediato su incumplimiento.  
El Juez fijará una distancia mínima entre el inculpado y la persona protegida que no se podrá rebasar, bajo apercibimiento de incurrir en responsabilidad penal.  
4.	La medida de alejamiento podrá acordarse con independencia de que la persona afectada, o aquéllas a quienes se pretenda proteger, hubieran abandonado previamente el lugar.  
5.	El Juez podrá prohibir al inculpado toda clase de comunicación con la persona o personas que se indique, bajo apercibimiento de incurrir en responsabilidad penal.  
6.	Las medidas a que se refieren los apartados anteriores podrán acordarse acumulada o separadamente.

##### Artículo 65

De las medidas de suspensión de la patria potestad o la custodia de menores.  
El Juez podrá suspender para el inculpado por violencia de género el ejercicio de la patria potestad, guarda y custodia, acogimiento, tutela, curatela o guarda de hecho, respecto de los menores que dependan de él.  
Si no acordara la suspensión, el Juez deberá pronunciarse en todo caso sobre la forma en la que se ejercerá la patria potestad y, en su caso, la guarda y custodia, el acogimiento, la tutela, la curatela o la guarda de hecho de lo menores. Asimismo, adoptará las medidas necesarias para garantizar la seguridad, integridad y recuperación de los menores y de la mujer, y realizará un seguimiento periódico de su evolución.

##### Artículo 66

De la medida de suspensión del régimen de visitas, estancia, relación o comunicación con los menores.  
El Juez ordenará la suspensión del régimen de visitas, estancia, relación o comunicación del inculpado por violencia de género respecto de los menores que dependan de él. Si, en interés superior del menor, no acordara la suspensión, el Juez deberá pronunciarse en todo caso sobre la forma en que se ejercerá el régimen de estancia, relación o comunicación del inculpado por violencia de género respecto de los menores que dependan del mismo. Asimismo, adoptará las medidas necesarias para garantizar la seguridad, integridad y recuperación de los menores y de la mujer, a través de servicios de atención especializada, y realizará un seguimiento periódico de su evolución, en coordinación con dichos servicios.

##### Artículo 67

De la medida de suspensión del derecho a la tenencia, porte y uso de armas.  
El Juez podrá acordar, respecto de los inculpados en delitos relacionados con la violencia a que se refiere esta Ley, la suspensión del derecho a la tenencia, porte y uso de

armas, con la obligación de depositarlas en los términos establecidos por la normativa vigente.

##### Artículo 68. Garantías para la adopción de las medidas

Las medidas restrictivas de derechos contenidas en este capítulo deberán adoptarse mediante auto motivado en el que se aprecie su proporcionalidad y necesidad, y, en todo caso, con intervención del Ministerio Fiscal y respeto de los principios de contradicción, audiencia y defensa.

##### Artículo 69. Mantenimiento de las medidas de protección y seguridad

Las medidas de este capítulo podrán mantenerse tras la sentencia definitiva y durante la tramitación de los eventuales recursos que correspondiesen. En este caso, deberá hacerse constar en la sentencia el mantenimiento de tales medidas.

#### CAPÍTULO V

Del Fiscal contra la Violencia sobre la Mujer

##### Artículo 70. Funciones del Fiscal contra la Violencia sobre la Mujer

Se añade un artículo 18 quáter en la Ley 50/1981, de 30 de diciembre, reguladora del Estatuto Orgánico del Ministerio Fiscal, con la siguiente redacción:
«1. El Fiscal General del Estado nombrará, oído el Consejo Fiscal, como delegado, un Fiscal contra la Violencia sobre la Mujer, con categoría de Fiscal de Sala, que ejercerá las siguientes funciones:
a)	Practicar las diligencias a que se refiere el artículo 5 del Estatuto Orgánico del Ministerio Fiscal, e intervenir directamente en aquellos procesos penales de especial trascendencia apreciada por el Fiscal General del Estado, referentes a los delitos por actos de violencia de género comprendidos en el artículo 87 ter.1 de la Ley Orgánica del Poder Judicial.  
b)	Intervenir, por delegación del Fiscal General del Estado, en los procesos civiles comprendidos en el artículo 87 ter.2 de la Ley Orgánica del Poder Judicial.  
c)	Supervisar y coordinar la actuación de las Secciones contra la Violencia sobre la Mujer, y recabar informes de las mismas, dando conocimiento al Fiscal Jefe de las Fiscalías en que se integren.  
d)	Coordinar los criterios de actuación de las diversas Fiscalías en materias de violencia de género, para lo cual podrá proponer al Fiscal General del Estado la emisión de las correspondientes instrucciones.  
e)	Elaborar semestralmente, y presentar al Fiscal General del Estado, para su remisión a la Junta de Fiscales de Sala del Tribunal Supremo, y al Consejo Fiscal, un informe sobre los procedimientos seguidos y actuaciones practicadas por el Ministerio Fiscal en materia de violencia de género.  
2.	Para su adecuada actuación se le adscribirán los profesionales y expertos que sean necesarios para auxiliarlo de manera permanente u ocasional.»

##### Article 64

On measures of leaving the home, restraining order or suspension of communications.  
1. The Judge may order the mandatory departure of the accused of gender-based violence from the home in which he had been living or where the family unit has its residence, as well as the prohibition to return to it.  
2. The Judge, on an exceptional basis, may authorize the protected person to arrange, with an agency or public company where one exists and which includes among its activities the rental of housing, the exchange of the attributed use of the family home of which they are co-owners, for the use of another home, for the time and under the conditions to be determined.  
3. The Judge may prohibit the accused from approaching the protected person, which prevents him from approaching her in any place where she may be, as well as approaching her home, her place of work or any other place frequented by her.  
The use of instruments with appropriate technology may be agreed upon to verify immediately any breach thereof.  
The Judge shall establish a minimum distance between the accused and the protected person which may not be reduced, under warning of incurring criminal liability.  
4. The restraining measure may be agreed upon regardless of whether the affected person, or those whom it is intended to protect, had previously left the place.  
5. The Judge may prohibit the accused from all kinds of communication with the person or persons indicated, under warning of incurring criminal liability.  
6. The measures referred to in the preceding paragraphs may be agreed upon cumulatively or separately.

##### Article 65

On measures of suspension of parental authority or custody of minors.  
The Judge may suspend for the accused of gender-based violence the exercise of parental authority, guardianship and custody, foster care, tutorship, curatorship or de facto guardianship, with respect to minors who depend on him.  
If suspension is not agreed upon, the Judge must in any case rule on the manner in which parental authority and, where applicable, guardianship and custody, foster care, tutorship, curatorship or de facto guardianship of the minors shall be exercised. Likewise, he shall adopt the necessary measures to guarantee the safety, integrity and recovery of the minors and of the woman, and shall carry out periodic monitoring of their progress.

##### Article 66

On the measure of suspension of the visitation, stay, relationship or communication regime with minors.  
The Judge shall order the suspension of the visitation, stay, relationship or communication regime of the accused of gender-based violence with respect to the minors who depend on him. If, in the best interest of the minor, suspension is not agreed upon, the Judge must in any case rule on the manner in which the stay, relationship or communication regime of the accused of gender-based violence with respect to the minors who depend on him shall be exercised. Likewise, he shall adopt the necessary measures to guarantee the safety, integrity and recovery of the minors and of the woman, through specialized care services, and shall carry out periodic monitoring of their progress, in coordination with said services.

##### Article 67

On the measure of suspension of the right to possession, carrying and use of weapons.  
The Judge may agree, with respect to those accused of crimes related to the violence referred to in this Law, the suspension of the right to possession, carrying and use of

weapons, with the obligation to deposit them under the terms established by current regulations.

##### Article 68. Guarantees for the adoption of measures

The rights-restrictive measures contained in this chapter must be adopted by means of a reasoned order in which their proportionality and necessity are assessed, and, in all cases, with the intervention of the Public Prosecutor's Office and respect for the principles of adversarial proceedings, hearing and defense.

##### Article 69. Maintenance of protection and security measures

The measures of this chapter may be maintained after the final judgment and during the processing of any applicable appeals. In this case, the maintenance of such measures must be recorded in the judgment.

#### CHAPTER V

On the Prosecutor against Violence against Women

##### Article 70. Functions of the Prosecutor against Violence against Women

An article 18 quater is added to Law 50/1981, of 30 December, regulating the Organic Statute of the Public Prosecutor's Office, with the following wording:
«1. The State Attorney General shall appoint, after hearing the Fiscal Council, as delegate, a Prosecutor against Violence against Women, with the rank of Chamber Prosecutor, who shall exercise the following functions:
a) Carry out the proceedings referred to in article 5 of the Organic Statute of the Public Prosecutor's Office, and intervene directly in those criminal proceedings of special significance appreciated by the State Attorney General, concerning crimes for acts of gender-based violence included in article 87 ter.1 of the Organic Law of the Judiciary.  
b) Intervene, by delegation of the State Attorney General, in civil proceedings included in article 87 ter.2 of the Organic Law of the Judiciary.  
c) Supervise and coordinate the actions of the Sections against Violence against Women, and request reports from them, informing the Chief Prosecutor of the Prosecutor's Offices in which they are integrated.  
d) Coordinate the action criteria of the various Prosecutor's Offices in matters of gender-based violence, for which purpose he may propose to the State Attorney General the issuance of the corresponding instructions.  
e) Prepare biannually, and present to the State Attorney General, for transmission to the Board of Chamber Prosecutors of the Supreme Court, and to the Fiscal Council, a report on the proceedings followed and actions carried out by the Public Prosecutor's Office in matters of gender-based violence.  
2. For its adequate performance, the professionals and experts necessary to assist him on a permanent or occasional basis shall be assigned to him.»

Cinco. Se introduce una nueva letra m) en el artículo 49, apartado 1, de la Ley del Estatuto de los Trabajadores, texto refundido aprobado por Real Decreto Legislativo 1/1995, de 24 de marzo, con el contenido siguiente:

«No se computarán como faltas de asistencia, a los efectos del párrafo anterior, las ausencias debidas a huelga legal por el tiempo de duración de la misma, el ejercicio de actividades de representación legal de los trabajadores, accidente de trabajo, maternidad, riesgo durante el embarazo, enfermedades causadas por embarazo, parto o lactancia, licencias y vacaciones, enfermedad o accidente no laboral, cuando la baja haya sido acordada por los servicios sanitarios oficiales y tenga una duración de más de veinte días consecutivos, ni las motivadas por la situación física o psicológica derivada de violencia de género, acreditada por los servicios sociales de atención o servicios de salud, según proceda.»
Siete. Se modifica la letra b) del apartado 5 del artículo 55, de la Ley del Estatuto de los Trabajadores, texto refundido aprobado por Real Decreto Legislativo 1/1995, de 24 de marzo, con el siguiente contenido:
«b) El de las trabajadoras embarazadas, desde la fecha de inicio del embarazo hasta la del comienzo del período de suspensión a que se refiere la letra a); la de los trabajadores que hayan solicitado uno de los permisos a los que se refieren los

apartados 4 y 5 del artículo 37 de esta Ley, o estén disfrutando de ellos, o hayan solicitado la excedencia prevista en el apartado 3 del artículo 46 de la misma; y la de las trabajadoras víctimas de violencia de género por el ejercicio de los derechos de reducción o reordenación de su tiempo de trabajo, de movilidad geográfica, de cambio de centro de trabajo o de suspensión de la relación laboral, en los términos y condiciones reconocidos en esta Ley.»

Disposición adicional octava. Modificación de la Ley General de la Seguridad Social. Uno. Se añade un apartado 5 en el artículo 124 de la Ley General de la Seguridad Social, texto refundido aprobado por Real Decreto Legislativo 1/1994, de 20 de junio, con el siguiente contenido:
«5. El período de suspensión con reserva del puesto de trabajo, contemplado en el artículo 48.6 del Estatuto de los Trabajadores, tendrá la consideración de período de cotización efectiva a efectos de las correspondientes prestaciones de la Seguridad Social por jubilación, incapacidad permanente, muerte o supervivencia, maternidad y desempleo.»
Dos. Se modifica la letra e) del apartado 1.1, así como el apartado 1.2 del artículo 208 de la Ley General de la Seguridad Social, texto refundido aprobado por Real Decreto Legislativo 1/1994, de 20 de junio, con el siguiente contenido:
«1.1.e) Por resolución voluntaria por parte del trabajador, en los supuestos previstos en los artículos 40, 41.3, 49.1.m) y 50 del Estatuto de los Trabajadores. 1.2 Cuando se suspenda su relación laboral en virtud de expediente de regulación de empleo, o de resolución judicial adoptada en el seno de un procedimiento concursal, o en el supuesto contemplado en la letra n), del apartado 1 del artículo 45 del Estatuto de los Trabajadores.»
Tres. Se modifica el apartado 2 del artículo 210 de la Ley General de la Seguridad Social, texto refundido aprobado por Real Decreto Legislativo 1/1994, de 20 de junio, con el siguiente contenido:
«2. A efectos de determinación del período de ocupación cotizada a que se refiere el apartado anterior se tendrán en cuenta todas las cotizaciones que no hayan sido computadas para el reconocimiento de un derecho anterior, tanto de nivel contributivo como asistencial. No obstante, no se considerará como derecho anterior el que se reconozca en virtud de la suspensión de la relación laboral prevista en el artículo 45.1.n) del Estatuto de los Trabajadores. No se computarán las cotizaciones correspondientes al tiempo de abono de la prestación que efectúe la entidad gestora o, en su caso, la empresa, excepto cuando la prestación se perciba en virtud de la suspensión de la relación laboral prevista en el artículo 45.1.n) del Estatuto de los Trabajadores, tal como establece el artículo
124.5 de esta Ley.»
Cuatro. Se modifica el apartado 2 del artículo 231 de la Ley General de la Seguridad Social, texto refundido aprobado por Real Decreto Legislativo 1/1994, de 20 de junio, con el siguiente contenido:
«2. A los efectos previstos en este título, se entenderá por compromiso de actividad el que adquiera el solicitante o beneficiario de las prestaciones de buscar activamente empleo, aceptar una colocación adecuada y participar en acciones específicas de motivación, información, orientación, formación, reconversión o inserción profesional para incrementar su ocupabilidad, así como de cumplir las restantes obligaciones previstas en este artículo. Para la aplicación de lo establecido en el párrafo anterior el Servicio Público de Empleo competente tendrá en cuenta la condición de víctima de violencia de género, a efectos de atemperar, en caso necesario, el cumplimiento de las obligaciones que se deriven del compromiso suscrito.»
Cinco. Se introduce una nueva disposición adicional en la Ley General de la Seguridad Social, texto refundido aprobado por Real Decreto Legislativo 1/1994, de 20 de junio, con el siguiente contenido:

«Disposición adicional cuadragésima segunda. Acreditación de situaciones legales de desempleo. La situación legal de desempleo prevista en los artículos 208.1.1e) y 208.1.2 de la presente Ley, cuando se refieren, respectivamente, a los artículos 49.1 m) y 45.1
n) de la Ley del Estatuto de los Trabajadores, se acreditará por comunicación escrita del empresario sobre la extinción o suspensión temporal de la relación laboral, junto con la orden de protección a favor de la víctima o, en su defecto, junto con el informe del Ministerio Fiscal que indique la existencia de indicios sobre la condición de víctima de violencia de género.»

Disposición adicional novena. Modificación de la Ley de Medidas para la Reforma de la Función Pública. Uno. El apartado 3 del artículo 1 de la Ley 30/1984, de 2 de agosto, de Medidas para la Reforma de la Función Pública, tendrá la siguiente redacción:
«3. Se consideran bases del régimen estatutario de los funcionarios públicos, dictadas al amparo del artículo 149.1.18.ª de la Constitución, y en consecuencia aplicables al personal de todas las Administraciones Públicas, los siguientes preceptos: artículos: 3.2.e) y f); 6; 7; 8; 11; 12; 13.2, 3 y 4; 14.4 y 5; 16; 17; 18.1 a 5; 19.1 y 3; 20.1.a), b), párrafo primero, c), e), g) en sus párrafos primero a cuarto, e i),
2 y 3; 21; 22.1, a excepción de los dos últimos párrafos; 23; 24; 25; 26; 29, a
excepción del último párrafo de sus apartados 5, 6 y 7; 30.5; 31; 32; 33; disposiciones adicionales tercera, 2 y 3, cuarta, duodécima y decimoquinta; disposiciones transitoria segunda, octava y novena.»
Dos. Se añade un nuevo apartado 3 al artículo 17 de la Ley 30/1984, de 2 de agosto, de Medidas para la Reforma de la Función Pública. «3. En el marco de los Acuerdos que las Administraciones Públicas suscriban con la finalidad de facilitar la movilidad entre los funcionarios de las mismas, tendrán especial consideración los casos de movilidad geográfica de las funcionarias víctimas de violencia de género.»
Tres. Se añade una letra i) al apartado 1 del artículo 20 de la Ley 30/1984, de 2 de agosto, de Medidas para la Reforma de la Función Pública, con el siguiente contenido:
«i) La funcionaria víctima de violencia sobre la mujer que se vea obligada a abandonar el puesto de trabajo en la localidad donde venía prestando sus servicios, para hacer efectiva su protección o su derecho a la asistencia social integral, tendrá derecho preferente a ocupar otro puesto de trabajo propio de su Cuerpo o Escala y de análogas características que se encuentre vacante y sea de necesaria provisión. Cuatro. Se añade un nuevo apartado 8 en el artículo 29 de la Ley 30/1984, de 2 de agosto, de Medidas para la Reforma de la Función Pública, con el siguiente contenido:
«8. Excedencia por razón de violencia sobre la mujer funcionaria. Las funcionarias públicas víctimas de violencia de género, para hacer efectiva su protección o su derecho a la asistencia social integral, tendrán derecho a solicitar la situación de excedencia sin necesidad de haber prestado un tiempo mínimo de servicios previos y sin que resulte de aplicación ningún plazo de permanencia en la misma. Durante los seis primeros meses tendrán derecho a la reserva del puesto de trabajo que desempeñaran, siendo computable dicho período a efectos de ascensos, trienios y derechos pasivos. Esto no obstante, cuando de las actuaciones de tutela judicial resultase que la efectividad del derecho de protección de la víctima lo exigiere, se podrá prorrogar por períodos de tres meses, con un máximo de dieciocho, el período en el que, de acuerdo con el párrafo anterior, se tendrá derecho a la reserva del puesto de trabajo, con idénticos efectos a los señalados en dicho párrafo.»

Cinco. Se añade un nuevo apartado 5 al artículo 30 de la Ley 30/1984, de 2 de agosto, de Medidas para la Reforma de la Función Pública con el siguiente contenido:
«5. En los casos en los que las funcionarias víctimas de violencia de género tuvieran que ausentarse por ello de su puesto de trabajo, estas faltas de asistencia, totales o parciales, tendrán la consideración de justificadas por el tiempo y en las condiciones en que así lo determinen los servicios sociales de atención o salud, según proceda. Las funcionarias víctimas de violencia sobre la mujer, para hacer efectiva su protección o su derecho a la asistencia social integral, tendrán derecho a la reducción de la jornada con disminución proporcional de la retribución, o a la reordenación del tiempo de trabajo, a través de la adaptación del horario, de la aplicación del horario flexible o de otras formas de ordenación del tiempo de trabajo que sean aplicables, en los términos que para estos supuestos establezca la Administración Pública competente en cada caso.»

«Artículo 26. Juzgados de Primera Instancia e Instrucción, de lo Mercantil, de Violencia sobre la Mujer, de lo Penal, de lo Contencioso-Administrativo, de lo Social, de Menores y de Vigilancia Penitenciaria.»
Dos. Se modifica la rúbrica del capítulo V del título IV del libro I de la Ley Orgánica 6/1985, de 1 de julio, del Poder Judicial, que queda redactada de la siguiente forma:
«Capítulo V. De los Juzgados de Primera Instancia e Instrucción, de lo Mercantil, de lo Penal, de Violencia sobre la Mujer, de lo Contencioso-Administrativo, de lo Social, de Vigilancia Penitenciaria y de Menores.»
Tres. Se modifica el apartado 1 del artículo 87 de la Ley Orgánica 6/1985, de 1 de julio, del Poder Judicial, que queda redactado de la siguiente forma:
«Artículo 87. 1. Los Juzgados de Instrucción conocerán, en el orden penal:
a)	De la instrucción de las causas por delito cuyo enjuiciamiento corresponda a las Audiencias Provinciales y a los Juzgados de lo Penal, excepto de aquellas causas que sean competencia de los Juzgados de Violencia sobre la Mujer. b)	Les corresponde asimismo dictar sentencia de conformidad con la acusación en los casos establecidos por la Ley.

##### Article 72. Delegates of the Head of the Public Prosecutor's Office

A new wording is given to paragraph 5 of article 22 of Law 50/1981, of 30 December, regulating the Organic Statute of the Public Prosecutor's Office, which is worded as follows:
"5. In those Public Prosecutor's Offices where the number of cases of which it has knowledge so advises and provided that it is convenient for the organization of the service, following a report from the Fiscal Council, delegates of the Head may be appointed in order to assume the management and coordination functions specifically entrusted to them. The organic staffing structure shall determine the maximum number of delegates of the Head that may be appointed in each Public Prosecutor's Office. In any case, in each Public Prosecutor's Office there shall be a delegate of the Head who shall assume the management and coordination functions, in the terms provided in this paragraph, in matters of offences related to gender-based violence, crimes against the environment, and prison supervision, exclusively or shared with other matters. Such delegates shall be appointed and, where appropriate, relieved by resolution issued by the State Attorney General, upon a reasoned proposal from the respective Chief Prosecutor, after hearing the Prosecutor's Board. When the resolution of the State Attorney General is at variance with the proposal of the respective Chief Prosecutor, it must be reasoned. For the filling of these positions it shall be necessary, prior to the proposal of the corresponding Chief Prosecutor, to make a call among the Prosecutors on the staff. The proposal shall be accompanied by a list of the other Prosecutors who have applied for the position with submission of the merits alleged."
First additional provision. Pensions and assistance. 1. Whoever is convicted, by final judgment, of the commission of an intentional crime of homicide in any of its forms or of injuries, shall lose the status of beneficiary of the widow's pension that corresponds to him or her within the public pension system when the victim of such crimes was the person giving rise to the pension, unless, where appropriate, there is reconciliation between them. In such cases, the widow's pension that should have been recognized shall increase the orphan's pensions, if any, provided that such increase is established in the legislation regulating the Social Security scheme in question. 2. Whoever is convicted, by final judgment, of the commission of an intentional crime of homicide in any of its forms or of injuries when the person offended by the crime was his or her spouse or former spouse, or was or had been linked to him or her by an analogous relationship of affection, even without cohabitation, shall not be entitled, in any case, to the orphan's pension of which his or her children could be beneficiaries within the Public Pension System, unless, where appropriate, there has been reconciliation between them. 3. Whoever is convicted of an intentional crime of homicide in any of its forms, when the offended person was his or her spouse or former spouse or a person with whom he or she was or had been linked in a stable manner by an analogous relationship of affection, regardless of sexual orientation, for at least the two years prior to the time of death, shall not be considered a beneficiary, as an indirect victim, of the assistance provided for in Law 35/1995, of 11 December, on Assistance and Aid to Victims of Violent Crimes and Crimes against Sexual Freedom, unless they had common descendants, in which case mere cohabitation shall suffice. Second additional provision. Action protocols. The Government and the autonomous communities that have assumed competences in matters of justice shall organize, within the scope proper to each, the forensic services so that they have comprehensive forensic assessment units responsible for designing protocols for global and comprehensive action in cases of gender-based violence. These protocols must pay special attention to vicarious violence. Third additional provision. Amendment of the Organic Law regulating the Right to Education. One. Letters b) and g) of article 2 of Organic Law 8/1985, of 3 July, regulating the Right to Education, shall be worded as follows:
"b) Training in respect for fundamental rights and freedoms, equality between men and women and in the exercise of tolerance and freedom within the democratic principles of coexistence. g) Training for peace, cooperation and solidarity among peoples and for the prevention of conflicts and for their peaceful resolution and non-violence in all areas of personal, family and social life."
Two. Three new letters are incorporated in paragraph 1 of article 31 of Organic Law 8/1985, of 3 July, regulating the Right to Education, which shall be worded as follows:
"k) Women's organizations with presence throughout the territory of the State. l) The Women's Institute. m) Persons of recognized prestige in the fight to eradicate gender-based violence."
Three. Letter e) of paragraph 1 of article 32 of Organic Law 8/1985, of 3 July, regulating the Right to Education, shall be worded as follows:
"e) Provisions relating to the development of equality of rights and opportunities and the promotion of real and effective equality between men and women in education."
Four. Paragraph 1 of article 33 of Organic Law 8/1985, of 3 July, regulating the Right to Education, shall be worded as follows:
"1. The State School Council shall prepare and publish annually a report on the education system, which must include and assess the various aspects thereof, including the possible situation of violence exercised in the educational community. It shall also report on the measures that the educational Administrations establish in relation to the prevention of violence and the promotion of equality between men and women."
Five. A new seventh bullet point is included in paragraph 1 of article 56 of Organic Law 8/1985, of 3 July, regulating the Right to Education, with the following wording:
"–A person, elected by the members of the School Council of the Centre, who promotes educational measures that foster real and effective equality between men and women."
Six. A new letter m) is added to article 57 of Organic Law 8/1985, of 3 July, regulating the Right to Education, with the following wording:

"m) To propose measures and initiatives that favour coexistence in the centre, equality between men and women and the peaceful resolution of conflicts in all areas of personal, family and social life."
Fourth additional provision. Amendment of the Organic Law on the General Organization of the Education System. One. Letter b) of paragraph 1 of article 1 of Organic Law 1/1990, of 3 October, on the General Organization of the Education System, is amended and shall be worded as follows:
"b) Training in respect for fundamental rights and freedoms, equality between men and women and in the exercise of tolerance and freedom within the democratic principles of coexistence."
Two. Letter e) is amended and letter l) is added to paragraph 3 of article 2 of Organic Law 1/1990, of 3 October, on the General Organization of the Education System, which shall be worded as follows:
"e) The promotion of habits of democratic behaviour and skills and techniques in the prevention of conflicts and in their peaceful resolution. l) Training for the prevention of conflicts and for their peaceful resolution in all areas of personal, family and social life."
Three. Paragraph 3 of article 34 of Organic Law 1/1990, of 3 October, on the General Organization of the Education System, is amended and shall be worded as follows:
"3. The teaching methodology of specific vocational training shall promote the integration of scientific, technological and organizational content. It shall also encourage in the student the capacity to learn independently and to work in a team, as well as training in the prevention of conflicts and for their peaceful resolution in all areas of personal, family and social life."

Fifth additional provision. Amendment of the Organic Law on the Quality of Education. One. A new letter b) is added, with the consequent displacement of the current ones, and three new letters n), ñ) and o) in article 1 of Organic Law 10/2002, of 23 December, on the Quality of Education, with the following content:
"b) The elimination of obstacles that hinder full equality between men and women. n) Training in respect for fundamental rights and freedoms, equality between men and women and in the exercise of tolerance and freedom within the democratic principles of coexistence. ñ) Training for the prevention of conflicts and for their peaceful resolution and non-violence in all areas of personal, family and social life. o) The development of affective capacities."
Two. Two new letters e) and f) are added, with the consequent displacement of the current ones, in paragraph 2 of article 12 of Organic Law 10/2002, of 23 December, on the Quality of Education, with the following content:
"e) To exercise themselves in the prevention of conflicts and in their peaceful resolution. f) To develop their affective capacities."
Three. Three new letters b), c) and d) are added, with the consequent displacement of the current ones, in paragraph 2 of article 15 of Organic Law 10/2002, of 23 December, on the Quality of Education, with the following content:
"b) To acquire skills in the prevention of conflicts and in their peaceful resolution that allow them to function with autonomy in the family and domestic sphere, as well as in the social groups in which they interact. c) To understand and respect equality between the sexes. d) To develop their affective capacities."

Four. Three new letters b), c) and d) are added, with the consequent displacement of the current ones, in paragraph 2 of article 22 of Organic Law 10/2002, of 23 December, on the Quality of Education, with the following content:
"b) To know, value and respect the equality of opportunities of men and women. c) To relate to others without violence, resolving conflicts peacefully. d) To develop their affective capacities."
Five. Letter f) of paragraph 1 is amended and a new paragraph 5 is added to article 23 of Organic Law 10/2002, of 23 December, on the Quality of Education, which is worded as follows:
"1. f) Ethics and equality between men and women."
"5. The subject of Ethics shall include specific content on equality between men and women."
Six. Two new letters b) and c) are added, with the consequent displacement of the current ones, in paragraph 2 of article 34 of Organic Law 10/2002, of 23 December, on the Quality of Education, with the following content:
"b) To consolidate personal, social and moral maturity, which enables them to act in a responsible, autonomous manner and to foresee and resolve peacefully personal, family and social conflicts. c) To promote real and effective equality between men and women and to analyse and critically assess inequalities between them."
Seven. A new paragraph 3 is added to article 40 of Organic Law 10/2002, of 23 December, on the Quality of Education, with the following content:
"3. In order to promote effective equality between men and women, the educational Administrations shall ensure that all curricula and educational materials recognize the equal value of men and women and are prepared on the basis of non-discriminatory assumptions for women. They must also promote respect for equality of rights and obligations."
Eight. Two new letters e) and f) are added in paragraph 2 of article 52 of Organic Law 10/2002, of 23 December, on the Quality of Education, with the following content:
"e) To develop skills in the peaceful resolution of conflicts in personal, family and social relationships. f) To promote respect for the dignity of persons and equality between men and women."
Nine. Letter d) of article 56 of Organic Law 10/2002, of 23 December, on the Quality of Education, is amended and is worded as follows:
"d) The tutoring of students to direct their learning, transmit values to them and help them, in collaboration with parents, to overcome their difficulties and resolve their conflicts peacefully."
Ten. A new letter g) is added, with the consequent displacement of the current letter g) which shall become a new letter h), in paragraph 2 of article 81 of Organic Law 10/2002, of 23 December, on the Quality of Education, with the following content:
"g) A person who promotes educational measures that foster real and effective equality between men and women, resident in the city where the centre is located and elected by the School Council of the centre."
Eleven. Letter k) in paragraph 1 of article 82 of Organic Law 10/2002, of 23 December, on the Quality of Education, is amended and is worded as follows:
"k) To propose measures and initiatives that favour coexistence in the centre, equality between men and women and the peaceful resolution of conflicts in all areas of personal, family and social life."

Twelve. A new letter g) is added to paragraph 1 of article 105 of Organic Law 10/2002, of 23 December, on the Quality of Education, which is worded as follows:
"g) To ensure compliance with and application of educational measures and initiatives aimed at promoting real equality between women and men."
Sixth additional provision. Amendment of the General Advertising Law. One. Article 3, letter a), of Law 34/1988, of 11 November, General Advertising Law, is amended and shall be worded as follows:
"The following is unlawful:
a) Advertising that violates the dignity of the person or infringes the values and rights recognized in the Constitution, especially those referred to in its articles 18 and 20, paragraph 4. The foregoing provision shall be understood to include advertisements that present women in a degrading manner, either by using particularly and directly their body or parts thereof as a mere object unrelated to the product being promoted, or their image associated with stereotyped behaviours that violate the foundations of our legal system, contributing to generate the violence referred to in the Organic Law on comprehensive protection measures against gender-based violence."
Two. A new paragraph 1 bis is added to article 25 of Law 34/1988, of 11 November, General Advertising Law, with the following content:
"1 bis. When advertising is considered unlawful for affecting the degrading or discriminatory use of the image of women, the following may request the advertiser to cease and rectify it:
a) The Special Government Delegation against Violence against Women. b) The Women's Institute or its equivalent at the autonomous community level. c) Legally constituted associations whose sole objective is the defence of women's interests and which do not include for-profit legal persons as members. d) Holders of a legitimate right or interest."
Three. An additional provision is added to Law 34/1988, of 11 November, General Advertising Law, with the following content:
"The action for cessation when advertising is considered unlawful for affecting the degrading or discriminatory use of the image of women shall be exercised in the manner and under the terms provided in articles 26 and 29, except in matters of standing, which shall be held, in addition to the Public Prosecutor's Office, by the persons and Institutions referred to in article 25.1 bis of this Law."

Seventh additional provision. Amendment of the Law on the Workers' Statute. One. A new paragraph 7 is introduced in article 37 of the Law on the Workers' Statute, consolidated text approved by Royal Legislative Decree 1/1995, of 24 March, with the following content:
"7. The female worker who is a victim of gender-based violence shall have the right, in order to make effective her protection or her right to comprehensive social assistance, to the reduction of working hours with proportional reduction of salary or to the reorganization of working time, through the adaptation of the schedule, the application of flexible hours or other forms of organization of working time used in the company. These rights may be exercised under the terms established for these specific cases in collective agreements or in agreements between the company and workers' representatives, or according to the agreement between the company and the affected female worker. Failing that, the specification of these rights shall correspond to the female worker, with the rules established in the previous paragraph being applicable, including those relating to the resolution of discrepancies."

Two. A new paragraph 3 bis) is introduced in article 40 of the Law on the Workers' Statute, consolidated text approved by Royal Legislative Decree 1/1995, of 24 March, with the following content:
"3 bis) The female worker who is a victim of gender-based violence who is obliged to leave her job in the locality where she had been providing her services, in order to make effective her protection or her right to comprehensive social assistance, shall have preferential right to occupy another job, of the same professional group or equivalent category, that the company has vacant in any of its other work centres. In such cases, the company shall be obliged to inform the female worker of the vacancies existing at that time or those that may arise in the future. The transfer or change of work centre shall have an initial duration of six months, during which the company shall be obliged to reserve the job that the female worker previously held. After this period, the female worker may choose between returning to her previous job or continuing in the new one. In the latter case, the aforementioned reservation obligation shall lapse."
Three. A new letter n) is introduced in article 45, paragraph 1, of the Law on the Workers' Statute, consolidated text approved by Royal Legislative Decree 1/1995, of 24 March, with the following content:
"n) By decision of the female worker who is obliged to leave her job as a consequence of being a victim of gender-based violence."
Four. A new paragraph 6 is introduced in article 48 of the Law on the Workers' Statute, consolidated text approved by Royal Legislative Decree 1/1995, of 24 March, with the following content:
"6. In the case provided for in letter n) of paragraph 1 of article 45, the suspension period shall have an initial duration that may not exceed six months, unless the judicial protection proceedings show that the effectiveness of the victim's right to protection requires the continuation of the suspension. In this case, the judge may extend the suspension for periods of three months, with a maximum of eighteen months."
Five. A new letter m) is introduced in article 49, paragraph 1, of the Law on the Workers' Statute, consolidated text approved by Royal Legislative Decree 1/1995, of 24 March, with the following content:
"m) By decision of the female worker who is obliged to permanently leave her job as a consequence of being a victim of gender-based violence."

"b) That of pregnant female workers, from the date of commencement of pregnancy until the commencement of the suspension period referred to in letter a); that of workers who have requested one of the permits referred to in paragraphs 4 and 5 of article 37 of this Law, or are enjoying them, or have requested the leave of absence provided for in paragraph 3 of article 46 thereof; and that of female workers who are victims of gender-based violence for the exercise of the rights to reduction or reorganization of their working time, geographical mobility, change of work centre or suspension of the employment relationship, under the terms and conditions recognized in this Law."

"1.1.e) By voluntary termination by the worker, in the cases provided for in articles 40, 41.3, 49.1.m) and 50 of the Workers' Statute. 1.2 When their employment relationship is suspended by virtue of an employment regulation procedure, or by judicial resolution adopted in the context of insolvency proceedings, or in the case contemplated in letter n), of paragraph 1 of article 45 of the Workers' Statute."

"2. Contributions corresponding to the time of payment of the benefit made by the managing entity or, where appropriate, the company shall not be counted, except when the benefit is received by virtue of the suspension of the employment relationship provided for in article 45.1.n) of the Workers' Statute, as established in article
124.5 of this Law."

"2. For the purposes provided for in this title, commitment to activity shall be understood as that acquired by the applicant or beneficiary of benefits to actively seek employment, accept suitable employment and participate in specific actions of motivation, information, guidance, training, retraining or professional insertion to increase their employability, as well as to fulfil the other obligations provided for in this article. n) of the Law on the Workers' Statute, shall be accredited by written communication from the employer on the termination or temporary suspension of the employment relationship, together with the protection order in favour of the victim or, failing that, together with the report of the Public Prosecutor's Office indicating the existence of indications of the status of victim of gender-based violence."

"i) The female civil servant who is a victim of violence against women who is obliged to leave her job in the locality where she had been providing her services, in order to make effective her protection or her right to comprehensive social assistance, shall have preferential right to occupy another job proper to her Corps or Scale and of similar characteristics that is vacant and requires filling. Cinco. Se adiciona un nuevo párrafo en el apartado 3 en el artículo 211 de la Ley Orgánica 6/1985, de 1 de julio, del Poder Judicial, que queda redactado de la siguiente forma:
«Los Jueces de Violencia sobre la Mujer serán sustituidos por los Jueces de Instrucción o de Primera Instancia e Instrucción, según el orden que establezca la Sala de Gobierno del Tribunal Superior de Justicia respectivo.»
Disposición adicional undécima. Evaluación de la aplicación de la Ley. El Gobierno, en colaboración con las Comunidades Autónomas, a los tres años de la entrada en vigor de esta Ley Orgánica elaborará y remitirá al Congreso de los Diputados un informe en el que se hará una evaluación de los efectos de su aplicación en la lucha contra la violencia de género. Disposición adicional duodécima. Modificaciones de la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal. Se añade una disposición adicional cuarta a la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal con el contenido siguiente:
«1. Las referencias que se hacen al Juez de Instrucción y al Juez de Primera Instancia en los apartados 1 y 7 del artículo 544 ter de esta Ley, en la redacción dada por la Ley 27/2003, de 31 de julio, reguladora de la Orden de Protección de las Víctimas de la Violencia Doméstica se entenderán hechas, en su caso, al Juez de Violencia sobre la Mujer. 2. Las referencias que se hacen al Juez de Guardia en el título III del libro IV, y en los artículos 962 a 971 de esta Ley, se entenderán hechas, en su caso, al Juez de Violencia sobre la Mujer.»
Disposición adicional decimotercera. Dotación del Fondo. Con el fin de coadyuvar a la puesta en funcionamiento de los servicios establecidos en el artículo 19 de esta Ley, y garantizar la equidad interterritorial en su implantación, durante los dos años siguientes a la entrada en vigor de esta Ley se dotará un Fondo al que podrán acceder las Comunidades Autónomas, de acuerdo con los criterios objetivos que se determinen en la respectiva Conferencia Sectorial. Ello, no obstante, la Comunidad Autónoma del País Vasco y la Comunidad Foral de Navarra se regirán, en estos aspectos financieros, por sus regímenes especiales de Concierto Económico y de Convenio. Las Comunidades Autónomas, en uso de sus competencias, durante el año siguiente a la aprobación de esta Ley, realizarán un diagnóstico conjuntamente con las Administraciones Locales, sobre el impacto de la violencia de género en su Comunidad, así como una valoración de necesidades, recursos y servicios necesarios, para implementar el artículo 19 de esta Ley. La dotación del Fondo se hará de conformidad con lo que dispongan las respectivas Leyes de Presupuestos Generales del Estado. Disposición adicional decimocuarta. Informe sobre financiación. Sin perjuicio de la responsabilidad financiera de las Comunidades Autónomas, conforme a lo establecido en la Ley 21/2001, de 27 de diciembre, por la que se regulan las medidas fiscales y administrativas del nuevo sistema de financiación de las Comunidades Autónomas de régimen común y Ciudades con Estatuto de Autonomía, y de acuerdo con el principio de lealtad institucional en los términos del artículo 2.1.e) de la Ley Orgánica 8/1980, de 22 de septiembre, de Financiación de las Comunidades Autónomas, los Ministerios competentes, a propuesta de los órganos interterritoriales correspondientes, elaborarán informes sobre las repercusiones económicas de la aplicación de esta Ley. Dichos informes serán presentados

al Ministerio de Economía y Hacienda que los trasladará al Consejo de Política Fiscal y Financiera. Disposición adicional decimoquinta. Convenios en materia de vivienda. Mediante convenios con las Administraciones competentes, el Gobierno podrá promover procesos específicos de adjudicación de viviendas protegidas a las víctimas de violencia de género. Disposición adicional decimosexta. Coordinación de los Servicios Públicos de Empleo. En el desarrollo de la Ley 56/2003, de 16 de diciembre, de Empleo, se tendrá en cuenta la necesaria coordinación de los Servicios Públicos de Empleo, para facilitar el acceso al mercado de trabajo de las víctimas de violencia de género cuando, debido al ejercicio del derecho de movilidad geográfica, se vean obligadas a trasladar su domicilio y el mismo implique cambio de Comunidad Autónoma. Disposición adicional decimoséptima. Escolarización. Las Administraciones educativas adoptarán las medidas necesarias para garantizar la escolarización inmediata de los hijos en el supuesto de cambio de residencia motivados por violencia sobre la mujer. Disposición adicional decimoctava. Planta de los Juzgados de Violencia sobre la Mujer. Se añade un anexo XIII a la Ley 38/1988, de 28 de diciembre, de Demarcación y Planta Judicial, cuyo texto se incluye como anexo a la presente Ley Orgánica. Disposición adicional decimonovena. Fondo de garantía de pensiones de alimentos. En el marco de la protección contra la violencia económica en los términos previstos en esta ley, el Estado garantizará el pago de alimentos reconocidos e impagados a favor de los hijos e hijas menores de edad en convenio judicialmente aprobado o en resolución judicial, a través de una legislación específica que concretará el sistema de cobertura en dichos supuestos y que, en todo caso, tendrá en cuenta las circunstancias de las víctimas de violencia de género. Para reforzar las medidas de apoyo a las víctimas de violencia económica, el Gobierno modificará la regulación actual del Fondo de Garantía de Pensiones en el sentido de mejorar su accesibilidad, su eficacia y su dotación económica, a través de la modificación del Real Decreto 1618/ 2007, de 7 de diciembre, sobre organización y funcionamiento del Fondo de Garantía del Pago de Alimentos. Disposición adicional vigésima. Cambio de apellidos. El artículo 58 de la Ley del Registro Civil, de 8 de junio de 1957, queda redactado de la siguiente forma:
«2. Cuando se den circunstancias excepcionales, y a pesar de faltar los requisitos que señala dicho artículo, podrá accederse al cambio por Real Decreto a propuesta del Ministerio de Justicia, con audiencia del Consejo de Estado. En caso de que el solicitante de la autorización del cambio de sus apellidos sea objeto de violencia de género y en cualquier otro supuesto en que la urgencia de la situación así lo requiriera podrá accederse al cambio por Orden del Ministerio de Justicia, en los términos fijados por el Reglamento.»

Disposición adicional vigesimoprimera. Macroencuesta de violencia contra la mujer. La Delegación del Gobierno contra la Violencia de Género realizará y publicará los resultados de la Macroencuesta de violencia contra la mujer prevista en el artículo 29 de esta ley con una periodicidad mínima trienal. Disposición transitoria primera. Aplicación de medidas. Los procesos civiles o penales relacionados con la violencia de género que se encuentren en tramitación a la entrada en vigor de la presente Ley continuarán siendo competencia de los órganos que vinieran conociendo de los mismos hasta su conclusión por sentencia firme. Disposición transitoria segunda. Derecho transitorio. En los procesos sobre hechos contemplados en la presente Ley que se encuentren en tramitación a su entrada en vigor, los Juzgados o Tribunales que los estén conociendo podrán adoptar las medidas previstas en el capítulo IV del título V. Disposición derogatoria única. Quedan derogadas cuantas normas, de igual o inferior rango, se opongan a lo establecido en la presente Ley. Disposición final primera. Referencias normativas. Todas las referencias y menciones contenidas en las leyes procesales penales a los Jueces de Instrucción deben también entenderse referidas a los Jueces de Violencia sobre la Mujer en las materias propias de su competencia. Disposición final segunda. Habilitación competencial. La presente Ley se dicta al amparo de lo previsto en el artículo 149.1, 1.ª, 5.ª, 6.ª, 7.ª, 8.ª, 17.ª, 18.ª y 30.ª de la Constitución Española. Disposición final tercera. Naturaleza de la presente Ley. La presente Ley tiene el carácter de Ley Orgánica, a excepción de los siguientes preceptos: título I, título II, título III, artículos 42, 43, 44, 45, 46, 47, 70, 71, 72, así como las disposiciones adicionales primera, segunda, sexta, séptima, octava, novena, undécima, decimotercera, decimoquinta, decimosexta, decimoséptima, decimoctava, decimonovena y vigésima, la disposición transitoria segunda y las disposiciones finales cuarta, quinta y sexta. Disposición final cuarta. Habilitación normativa. 1. Se habilita al Gobierno para que dicte, en el plazo de seis meses a partir de la publicación de esta Ley en el «Boletín Oficial del Estado», las disposiciones que fueran necesarias para su aplicación. A través del Ministerio de Justicia se adoptarán en el referido plazo las medidas necesarias para la implantación de los Juzgados de Violencia sobre la Mujer, así como para la adecuación de la estructura del Ministerio Fiscal a las previsiones de la presente Ley. 2. En el plazo de seis meses desde la entrada en vigor de la presente Ley Orgánica el Consejo General del Poder Judicial dictará los reglamentos necesarios para la ordenación de los señalamientos, adecuación de los servicios de guardia a la existencia de los nuevos Juzgados de Violencia sobre la Mujer, y coordinación de la Policía Judicial con los referidos Juzgados. Disposición final quinta. Modificaciones reglamentarias. El Gobierno, en el plazo de seis meses desde la aprobación de esta Ley, procederá a la modificación del artículo 116.4 del Real Decreto 190/1996, de 9 de febrero, por el que se aprueba el Reglamento Penitenciario, estableciendo la obligatoriedad para la Administración Penitenciaria de realizar los programas específicos de tratamiento para internos a que se refiere la presente Ley. En el mismo plazo se procederá a modificar el Real Decreto 738/1997, de 23 de mayo, por el que se aprueba el Reglamento de ayudas a las víctimas de delitos violentos y contra la libertad sexual, y el Real Decreto 996/2003, de 25 de julio, por el que se aprueba el Reglamento de asistencia jurídica gratuita. En el plazo mencionado en el apartado anterior, el Estado y las Comunidades Autónomas, en el ámbito de sus respectivas competencias, adaptarán su normativa a las previsiones contenidas en la presente Ley. Disposición final sexta. Modificación de la Ley 1/1996, de 10 de enero, de Asistencia Jurídica Gratuita. Se modifica el apartado 5 del artículo 3 de la Ley 1/1996, de 10 de enero, de Asistencia Gratuita, que quedará redactado como sigue:
«5. Tampoco será necesario que las víctimas de violencia de género acrediten previamente carecer de recursos cuando soliciten defensa jurídica gratuita especializada, que se les prestará de inmediato, sin perjuicio de que si no se le reconoce con posterioridad el derecho a la misma, éstas deban abonar al abogado los honorarios devengados por su intervención.»

Three bis. A new paragraph is added to section 2 of article 89 bis of the Organic Law of the Judiciary, with the following content:

"In order to facilitate the hearing of cases investigated by the Courts of Violence against Women, and taking into account the number of existing cases, one or more Courts in each province must be specialized, in accordance with the provisions of article 98 of this Law."

Four. Section 1 of article 210 of Organic Law 6/1985, of 1 July, of the Judiciary, is amended to read as follows:

"1. The Judges of First Instance and Investigation, Commercial, Criminal, Violence against Women, Administrative, Minors and Social Courts shall substitute for each other in localities where there are several of the same jurisdictional order, in the manner agreed by the Governing Chamber of the High Court of Justice, at the proposal of the Board of Judges."

Five. A new paragraph is added to section 3 of article 211 of Organic Law 6/1985, of 1 July, of the Judiciary, which reads as follows:

"The Judges of Violence against Women shall be substituted by the Investigating Judges or First Instance and Investigation Judges, according to the order established by the Governing Chamber of the respective High Court of Justice."

Eleventh additional provision. Evaluation of the application of the Law.

The Government, in collaboration with the Autonomous Communities, three years after the entry into force of this Organic Law, shall prepare and submit to the Congress of Deputies a report evaluating the effects of its application in the fight against gender-based violence.

Twelfth additional provision. Amendments to the Criminal Procedure Law.

A fourth additional provision is added to the Criminal Procedure Law with the following content:

"1. The references made to the Investigating Judge and the First Instance Judge in sections 1 and 7 of article 544 ter of this Law, in the wording given by Law 27/2003, of 31 July, regulating the Protection Order for Victims of Domestic Violence, shall be understood as made, where applicable, to the Judge of Violence against Women.

2. The references made to the Duty Judge in title III of book IV, and in articles 962 to 971 of this Law, shall be understood as made, where applicable, to the Judge of Violence against Women."

Thirteenth additional provision. Funding of the Fund.

In order to contribute to the implementation of the services established in article 19 of this Law, and to guarantee inter-territorial equity in their implementation, during the two years following the entry into force of this Law, a Fund shall be established to which the Autonomous Communities may have access, in accordance with the objective criteria to be determined in the respective Sectoral Conference. Notwithstanding this, the Autonomous Community of the Basque Country and the Foral Community of Navarre shall be governed, in these financial aspects, by their special regimes of Economic Agreement and Convention.

The Autonomous Communities, in the exercise of their powers, during the year following the approval of this Law, shall carry out a diagnosis jointly with the Local Administrations, on the impact of gender-based violence in their Community, as well as an assessment of needs, resources and services necessary to implement article 19 of this Law.

The allocation of the Fund shall be made in accordance with the provisions of the respective General State Budget Laws.

Fourteenth additional provision. Report on financing.

Without prejudice to the financial responsibility of the Autonomous Communities, in accordance with the provisions of Law 21/2001, of 27 December, regulating the fiscal and administrative measures of the new financing system for the Autonomous Communities of common regime and Cities with Statute of Autonomy, and in accordance with the principle of institutional loyalty in the terms of article 2.1.e) of Organic Law 8/1980, of 22 September, on Financing of the Autonomous Communities, the competent Ministries, at the proposal of the corresponding inter-territorial bodies, shall prepare reports on the economic repercussions of the application of this Law. These reports shall be submitted

to the Ministry of Economy and Finance, which shall forward them to the Fiscal and Financial Policy Council.

Fifteenth additional provision. Agreements on housing matters.

Through agreements with the competent Administrations, the Government may promote specific processes for the allocation of protected housing to victims of gender-based violence.

Sixteenth additional provision. Coordination of Public Employment Services.

In the development of Law 56/2003, of 16 December, on Employment, the necessary coordination of the Public Employment Services shall be taken into account, to facilitate access to the labour market for victims of gender-based violence when, due to the exercise of the right to geographical mobility, they are obliged to relocate their domicile and this implies a change of Autonomous Community.

Seventeenth additional provision. School enrolment.

The educational authorities shall adopt the necessary measures to guarantee the immediate school enrolment of children in the event of a change of residence motivated by violence against women.

Eighteenth additional provision. Structure of the Courts of Violence against Women.

An annex XIII is added to Law 38/1988, of 28 December, on Judicial Demarcation and Structure, the text of which is included as an annex to this Organic Law.

Nineteenth additional provision. Maintenance payment guarantee fund.

Within the framework of protection against economic violence in the terms provided for in this law, the State shall guarantee the payment of recognised and unpaid maintenance in favour of minor children in judicially approved agreements or in judicial resolutions, through specific legislation that shall specify the coverage system in such cases and which, in any event, shall take into account the circumstances of victims of gender-based violence.

To strengthen support measures for victims of economic violence, the Government shall modify the current regulation of the Maintenance Payment Guarantee Fund in order to improve its accessibility, effectiveness and financial allocation, through the amendment of Royal Decree 1618/2007, of 7 December, on the organisation and operation of the Maintenance Payment Guarantee Fund.

Twentieth additional provision. Change of surnames.

Article 58 of the Civil Registry Law, of 8 June 1957, reads as follows:

"2. When exceptional circumstances exist, and despite the absence of the requirements indicated in that article, the change may be granted by Royal Decree at the proposal of the Ministry of Justice, with the hearing of the Council of State. In the event that the applicant for authorisation to change their surnames is a victim of gender-based violence and in any other case where the urgency of the situation so requires, the change may be granted by Order of the Ministry of Justice, in the terms established by the Regulations."

Twenty-first additional provision. Macro-survey on violence against women.

The Government Delegation against Gender-based Violence shall conduct and publish the results of the Macro-survey on violence against women provided for in article 29 of this law with a minimum three-yearly frequency.

First transitional provision. Application of measures.

Civil or criminal proceedings related to gender-based violence that are in progress at the entry into force of this Law shall continue to be the competence of the bodies that have been hearing them until their conclusion by final judgment.

Second transitional provision. Transitional law.

In proceedings concerning facts contemplated in this Law that are in progress at its entry into force, the Courts or Tribunals hearing them may adopt the measures provided for in chapter IV of title V.

Sole derogatory provision.

All provisions, of equal or lower rank, that are contrary to the provisions of this Law are hereby repealed.

First final provision. Regulatory references.

All references and mentions contained in criminal procedural laws to Investigating Judges must also be understood as referring to Judges of Violence against Women in matters within their competence.

Second final provision. Competence authorisation.

This Law is enacted pursuant to the provisions of article 149.1, 1st, 5th, 6th, 7th, 8th, 17th, 18th and 30th of the Spanish Constitution.

Third final provision. Nature of this Law.

This Law has the character of an Organic Law, with the exception of the following provisions: title I, title II, title III, articles 42, 43, 44, 45, 46, 47, 70, 71, 72, as well as the first, second, sixth, seventh, eighth, ninth, eleventh, thirteenth, fifteenth, sixteenth, seventeenth, eighteenth, nineteenth and twentieth additional provisions, the second transitional provision and the fourth, fifth and sixth final provisions.

Fourth final provision. Regulatory authorisation.

1. The Government is authorised to issue, within six months from the publication of this Law in the "Official State Gazette", the provisions necessary for its application. Through the Ministry of Justice, the necessary measures shall be adopted within the aforementioned period for the implementation of the Courts of Violence against Women, as well as for the adaptation of the structure of the Public Prosecutor's Office to the provisions of this Law.

2. Within six months from the entry into force of this Organic Law, the General Council of the Judiciary shall issue the necessary regulations for the organisation of hearings, adaptation of on-call services to the existence of the new Courts of Violence against Women, and coordination of the Judicial Police with the aforementioned Courts.

Fifth final provision. Regulatory amendments.

The Government, within six months from the approval of this Law, shall proceed to amend article 116.4 of Royal Decree 190/1996, of 9 February, approving the Penitentiary Regulations, establishing the obligation for the Penitentiary Administration to carry out the specific treatment programmes for inmates referred to in this Law.

Within the same period, Royal Decree 738/1997, of 23 May, approving the Regulations on aid to victims of violent crimes and crimes against sexual freedom, and Royal Decree 996/2003, of 25 July, approving the Regulations on free legal assistance, shall be amended.

Within the period mentioned in the previous paragraph, the State and the Autonomous Communities, within the scope of their respective powers, shall adapt their regulations to the provisions contained in this Law.

Sixth final provision. Amendment of Law 1/1996, of 10 January, on Free Legal Assistance.

Section 5 of article 3 of Law 1/1996, of 10 January, on Free Assistance, is amended to read as follows:

"5. Nor shall it be necessary for victims of gender-based violence to prove in advance that they lack resources when they request specialised free legal defence, which shall be provided to them immediately, without prejudice to the fact that if the right thereto is not subsequently recognised, they must pay the lawyer the fees accrued for their intervention."

Seventh final provision. Entry into force.

This Organic Law shall enter into force thirty days after its publication in the "Official State Gazette", except for the provisions of titles IV and V, which shall do so after six months.

Therefore,

I command all Spaniards, individuals and authorities, to observe and enforce this organic law.

Madrid, 28 December 2004.

JUAN CARLOS R.

The President of the Government,
